correctness.rationale: Substituting quarter flux and the commensurate lengths into the source high-energy criterion reduces the periodic indicator to the sign of \(-\cos((2m+1)x)\sin(mx)\sin((m+1)x)\). On half a period, the zero sets interlace; pairing the alternating jumps with cosine half-grid jumps gives a mismatch length equal to the two explicit absolute-value sums. Evaluating those sums separately for even and odd m yields the stated formula. Away from fixed neighborhoods of the finitely many period zeros, the source's relative \(O(k^{-2})\) correction is uniformly negligible; shrinking the neighborhoods proves equality of asymptotic densities. The source symmetric formula gives 1/2 at quarter flux. A fresh independent exact-rational interval calculation matched the closed form for every \(1\le m\le50\).

value.rationale: The source explicitly identifies commensurate ratios as the nonuniversal unresolved regime. This theorem gives an infinite exact rational family, a sharp \(m^{-2}\) defect, and a discontinuity at the symmetric geometry despite converging lengths, which is a motivated structural phenomenon rather than an isolated computation.

final_claim: At quarter flux in the tightly connected magnetic ring chain, for the adjacent commensurate arc ratio \(m/(m+1)\), the positive high-energy momentum-band density is \(P_m=3/4-[4(2m+1)s_m]^{-1}\), where \(s_m\) is the odd member of \(\{m,m+1\}\); hence \(P_m\to3/4\) while the exactly symmetric ratio has density \(1/2\).
